content: The acetanilide form is in, and its QED of 0.9116 is actually higher than the cyclopropyl version I am heading for - worth noting, because it means the cap swap is a trade rather than a free win. But the acetyl costs about 0.10 of activity against a cycloalkyl, and at this activity level that is far more than the couple of hundredths of QED it returns. Atom 1 is the amide carbonyl and atom 0 the acetyl methyl over a non-ring bond, so I swap the methyl for a cyclopropyl. That gives N-{3-[(4-bromopyridin-2-yl)amino]phenyl}cyclopropanecarboxamide, the best molecule found in three runs at jnk3 0.60 and Phi 2.3799. Getting it into the population on the first episode means the next two generations refine from there rather than searching, which is what turned run 3 into an improvement on run 2.
